applyRuleButton: {count, plural, one {Apply to # message} other {Apply to # messages}}
ruleRanDone: {count, plural, =0 {No message was changed.} one {Applied to # message.} other {Applied to # messages.}}
ruleRanWaiting: {count, plural, one {# waits for the server.} other {# wait for the server.}}

ruleLogIntro: Each time a rule acts on a message, it is listed here, newest first. Undo puts the message back as it was.
pauseAndUndoEllipsis: Pause and undo everything it did…
ruleLogEmpty: Nothing yet. When a rule acts on new mail, it shows here.

@entryLine.description: Under an entry's subject in the activity log: who sent the message, the rule, and when it acted.

pauseAndUndoNamed: Pause “{name}” and undo everything it did…
rulePausedNote: “{name}” is paused: it sorts no new mail. What it did stays as it is.
pauseUndoTitle: Pause “{name}” and undo everything it did?
pauseUndoMessage: It stops sorting new mail, and every change it made that is not undone yet is put back: the messages it moved go back where they were, and its stars, read marks and labels are taken back. A message moved since by something else stays where it is.
undoAllMessage: Every change it made that is not undone yet is put back: the messages it moved go back where they were, and its stars, read marks and labels are taken back. A message moved since by something else stays where it is.
pauseUndoDone: “{name}” is paused, and {count, plural, =0 {it had nothing left to undo} one {# change was undone} other {# changes were undone}}.
undoAllDone: {count, plural, =0 {“{name}” had nothing left to undo.} one {# change by “{name}” was undone.} other {# changes by “{name}” were undone.}}
undoAllFailed: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing “{name}” did could be undone: {error}} one {# change by “{name}” was undone, but not all: {error}} other {# changes by “{name}” were undone, but not all: {error}}}
makeRuleEllipsis: Make a rule from this message…
securityPassedDetail: The receiving server verified this message's sender with SPF, DKIM or DMARC. That says where it came from, not that it is safe.
securityFailedDetail: The receiving server reported that a sender check failed. The message may not come from the address it shows.
securityAbsentDetail: The receiving server reported no sender verification. Treat unexpected mail with care.
securityExternalDetail: {email} is outside your organization's domains. Most mail is, but check unexpected requests for money or passwords.

@securityExternalDetail.description: Explains an external sender without calling the message malicious.

securityReplyMismatchDetail: The message is from {from}, but replies would go to {replyTo}. Check that address before answering.

@securityReplyMismatchDetail.description: Explains a Reply-To that leaves the sender's domain.

@securityChecks.description: The SPF, DKIM and DMARC results a server reported.

@securityLinkMessage.description: Shows the real destination of a link before it opens.

securityAttachmentTypeMismatch: Content does not match the name

@renameFolderTitle.description: The title of the form that renames a folder.

@deleteFolderTitle.description: The title of the confirmation before a folder is deleted.

deleteFolderConfirm: This deletes the folder “{name}” and the {count, plural, one {message} other {# messages}} in it. This cannot be undone.

@deleteFolderConfirm.description: Says that deleting a folder also deletes its mail.

@folderCreated.description: The note after a folder was created.

@folderRenamed.description: The note after a folder was renamed.

@folderDeleted.description: The note after a folder was deleted.

@folderActionFailed.description: The error after a folder action failed.

@folderHidden.description: The note after a folder was hidden.

@folderShown.description: The note after a folder was shown again.

@movedToFolder.description: The note after messages were moved to a folder. On the undo banner.

folderExists: A folder of that name already exists.
folderBadName: That name cannot be used: it is empty, has control characters, or starts or ends with the folder separator.
folderSystem: The inbox and the Sent, Drafts, Archive, Junk and Trash folders cannot be renamed or deleted.
networkIntro: How Shu reaches your mail servers and model providers. Changes apply to the next connection; no restart is needed.
proxyPasswordStored: A password is stored. Leave it empty to keep it.
certificateAuthorityHint: Trust an internal or self-signed authority from a PEM file. Certificate checks stay on.

caInvalid: That file holds no certificate Shu can read.
networkSaveFailed: Could not save the network settings: {error}

@networkSaveFailed.description: The error after saving the network settings failed.

networkTestOk: The connection works through these settings.

@networkTestFailed.description: The error after a network test failed.

networkNoAccount: Add an account to test the connection.
imagesBlockedDetail: This message shows pictures from the network. They are not loaded, so the sender cannot tell that you read it.
imagesShownDetail: Remote images from this message are shown.
imagesFailed: Could not change the image setting: {error}

@imagesFailed.description: The error after allowing or blocking remote images failed.

@previewAttachment.description: The button that opens an attachment preview.

previewUnavailable: There is no preview for this kind of file.

@previewFailed.description: The error after reading an attachment for preview failed.

@saveAllFailed.description: The note after Save all had failures.

saveAllNoFolder: Choose a folder to save the attachments in.
transferIntro: Bring mail in from mbox or .eml files, take it out, or back up the account settings. Imports upload to the folder open in the mail window; secrets are never exported.
transferNoFolder: Open a mail folder before importing or exporting.

transferImportedSkipped: {count, plural, one {Imported # message} other {Imported # messages}}, skipped {skipped}

@transferExported.description: The note after an export finished.

transferNoSelection: Choose at least one message to export.
shortcutsIntro: These work anywhere in the mail window. They never fire while you are typing in a field.
inviteUpdated: This is an update to the invitation

@inviteYourResponse.description: The user's response to an invitation.

@inviteReplySent.description: The note after an RSVP was sent.

@inviteReplyFailed.description: The error after an RSVP failed.

inviteUnreadable: This message has a meeting invitation Shu cannot read.
inviteAddOpened: Opened the event in your calendar app

@inviteAddFailed.description: The error after opening an event failed.

inviteNoReply: This invitation has no organizer to answer.
aiLocalToolIntro: Use a Claude Code or Codex command already signed in on this Mac. Shu never reads or stores its credentials; the mail text is sent by that tool to its vendor under their terms.
aiLocalToolPathHint: Empty finds the command the way Terminal does. A set path that does not run is an error, never a fallback.

@aiLocalToolVersion.description: The version of an installed local AI command.

aiLocalToolIsolation: Runs in a private empty folder, with tools, plugins and hooks off where the tool allows it. The prompt goes in on standard input, never on the command line.
aiCliEnvHint: Set for this tool only, each time it starts. Values stay in the login Keychain.

@aiCliEnvRemove.description: The button that removes one environment variable.

aiCliEnvReserved: Shu sets that name itself, so a value is not used.

@aiCliEnvFailed.description: The error after saving a tool's environment failed.

aiProvidersIntro: Installed tools and API connections, and the models each one offers.
aiProviderModelDefault: The chosen model always stays visible.
aiProviderNoModels: This provider reports no models yet. Type one below.
aiProviderModelHint: Type a model, or choose one this provider reports.
aiProviderOffHint: Its models leave the pickers. Its setup and key are kept.
aiProviderKeyMoved: This key was saved for another server. Save it again for this one.
aiProviderRemoveHint: Deletes this provider’s setup from this device, its keychain entries included. Mail and drafts stay.

@aiProviderRemoveTitle.description: The title that asks before a provider's setup is deleted.

aiProviderRemoveKey: Shu forgets this provider's setup and deletes its API key from the login Keychain. Mail, drafts and summaries stay, and adding the provider again starts from an empty setup.
aiProviderRemoveTool: Shu forgets this provider's setup and deletes its keychain entries: the {count, plural, one {value it was given} other {# values it was given}}. The tool itself, its sign-in and its files stay untouched, and adding it again starts from an empty setup.

@aiProviderRemoveTool.description: The message before a local tool's setup is deleted; it names how many keychain values go.

@aiProviderRemoved.description: The note after a provider's setup was deleted.

@aiLocalToolAccount.description: The account a local tool reports it is signed in as.

@aiLocalToolCopied.description: Confirms the sign-in command is on the clipboard.

aiLocalToolNotOfficial: Shu is not affiliated with the tools’ vendors, and this is not an official integration. Using a subscription through another app may be restricted by the vendor’s terms; check them before relying on it.

@aiProviderModelsCount.description: How many models a connection offers.

aiProviderModelsHint: Choose the models this connection offers.
aiProviderNoModelsYet: No models yet — fetch or add one by ID.

blockFolderCaption: Send the sender's new mail to

blockNoFolder: This account has no Junk or Trash folder to file the sender's mail in.
